blocks.task_summary: Sketch y=f(x)=x³−3cx+2 for c=1, showing y-intercept and points with zero gradient.

evidence.basis: positive cubic with correct y-intercept labelled (A1); local maximum point correctly labelled (A1); local minimum point correctly labelled (A1) [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Sketch y=f(x)=x³−3cx+2 for c=2, showing y-intercept and points with zero gradient.

evidence.basis: positive cubic with correct y-intercept labelled (A1); local maximum point correctly labelled (A1); local minimum point correctly labelled (A1). Note: Accept exact answers: Local maximum (−√2, 2+4√2), Local minimum (√2, 2−4√2). [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Write down an expression for f′(x).
Find the set of values of c such that the graph has a point of inflexion with zero gradient.
method_path: For inflexion with zero gradient, f″(x)=0 ⇒ x=0 and f′(0)=0 ⇒ −3c=0
accepted_alternatives: Condition that f′(x)=0 has a double root, discriminant = 0 ⇒ c=0

blocks.task_summary: Find the set of values of c such that the graph has one local maximum and one local minimum point.
method_path: For two distinct real stationary points, require c > 0
accepted_alternatives: Considers the number of solutions to f′(x)=0; the M1 can be awarded for work shown in either (ii) or (iii)

evidence.basis: considers the number of solutions to their f′(x)=0 (M1); c>0 (A1) [2 marks]. Note: The (M1) in part (c)(ii) can be awarded for work shown in either (ii) or (iii).

blocks.task_summary: Find the set of values of c such that the graph has no points where the gradient is zero.
method_path: For no real solutions, require c < 0

blocks.task_summary: Show that the y-coordinate of the local maximum point is 2c^(3/2)+2.
accepted_alternatives: Award credit if work seen in part (c); accept if either x=−√c or x=√c is subsequently considered

evidence.basis: attempts to solve their f′(x)=0 for x (M1); x=±√c (A1) — Note: Award (A1) if either x=−√c or x=√c is subsequently considered; correctly evaluates f(−√c) (A1); the y-coordinate of the local maximum point is 2c^(3/2)+2 AG. [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Show that the y-coordinate of the local minimum point is −2c^(3/2)+2.

evidence.basis: correctly evaluates f(√c) (A1); the y-coordinate of the local minimum point is −2c^(3/2)+2 AG. [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: For c>0, find the set of values of c such that the graph has exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: Local minimum y-coordinate must be above x-axis
accepted_alternatives: Rigorous reasoning that the minimum point is above the x-axis; accept c<1 (condoned) as c>0 is given

evidence.basis: the graph of y=f(x) will have one x-axis intercept if 2−2c^(3/2)>0 (or equivalent reasoning) (R1); 0<c<1 (A1). Note: Condone c<1. The A1 is independent of the R1. [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: For c>0, find the set of values of c such that the graph has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: Local minimum y-coordinate must equal zero (touches x-axis)
accepted_alternatives: Evidence from the graph in part (a)(i) where c=1 gives exactly two intercepts

evidence.basis: the graph will have two x-axis intercepts if 2−2c^(3/2)=0 (or equivalent reasoning, or evidence from graph in part (a)(i)) (M1); c=1 (A1). [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: For c>0, find the set of values of c such that the graph has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: Local minimum y-coordinate must be below x-axis
accepted_alternatives: Reasoning from the results in both parts (e)(i) and (e)(ii)

evidence.basis: the graph will have three x-axis intercepts if 2−2c^(3/2)<0 (or equivalent reasoning, or reasoning from results in both (e)(i) and (e)(ii)) (M1); c>1 (A1). [2 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find all conditions on c and d such that g(x)=x³−3cx+d has exactly one x-axis intercept, explaining reasoning.
method_path: Case 1: c ≤ 0 → g′(x)=3x²−3c has at most one real root, no two distinct stationary points, so exactly one x-intercept for any d∈ℝ
Case 2: c > 0 → stationary points at x=±√c with y-values: local max at (−√c, 2c^(3/2)+d), local min at (√c, −2c^(3/2)+d)
For exactly one intercept, both stationary points must lie on the same side of the x-axis
accepted_alternatives: Case 1 reasoning alternatives: g′(x)=0 does not have two solutions; OR g′(x) ≥ 0 for all x∈ℝ; OR graph of y=f(x) has no local max/min, hence any vertical translation also has none. Case 2 alternative: consider only local minimum above x-axis OR only local maximum below x-axis instead of both conditions.

evidence.basis: Case 1: c ≤ 0 (independent of d) (A1). EITHER g′(x)=0 does not have two solutions R1; OR g′(x) ≥ 0 for x∈ℝ R1; OR graph has no local max/min, any vertical translation also has none R1. Therefore only one x-axis intercept AG. Note: Award at most A0R1 if only c<0 is considered.

Case 2: c>0. (−√c, 2c^(3/2)+d) local max and (√c, −2c^(3/2)+d) local min (A1). Considers positions of local max and/or local min (M1). d > 2c^(3/2) (both above x-axis) A1; d < −2c^(3/2) (both below x-axis) A1. Note: Award at most (A1)(M1)A0A0 if c>0 not clearly stated. [6 marks]
